text:
sarah chen: heads up, CI started failing on the hotfix pipeline ~04:12 UTC. multiple jobs can't pull packages from ghcr/registry, 502/503 from the package registry. blocking the rollback build.
maria lopez: seeing the same in agent-hotfix-3 logs. primary error: `GET https://ghcr.io/v2/redwood-inference/node-mods/blobs/sha256:... 502` then action times out.
sarah chen: pasted the failing step logs below:
```
Attempting to download package: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/node-mods:1.2.3
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
2026-03-15T04:12:07Z | error | response: 502
Error: failed to fetch package after 3 attempts
```
oncall-bot: @sarah chen, you are the current oncall (pager duty). Incident created: INC-2026-03-15-01. Severity: high (blocking deploys).
tony nguyen: linking GitHub status — https://www.githubstatus.com/ reports degraded performance in Packages and Actions in us-east-1. :grimacing:
infra-sre-bot: auto-run: collecting failed job artifacts and runner diagnostics. Uploaded to s3://incidents/1930005555/diagnostics.tgz
maria lopez: quick impact summary — all hotfix builds that pull private packages from ghcr are failing; canary and prod deploys that rely on those artifacts are blocked. Surface customers on support: customers using Dedicated reserved capacity rollout today (5 customers) might be blocked from receiving the hotfix.
evan (product): copy for CS — we need a short blurb to send to affected customers. Is there a known ETA from GH?
tony nguyen: no ETA yet. GH status says 'under investigation'. We should prepare mitigation steps.
sarah chen: mitigation options I'm thinking of:
- try workflow-level fallback to npm registry mirror (registry.npmjs.org) for public packages
- for private packages, use temporary S3 artifact publish + direct install via tarball
- as a last resort, rebuild images with vendored node_modules and push to our docker registry
maria lopez: I can try a workflow patch right now in a branch: add a step before restore-cache that does `npm config set @redwood:registry https://registry.npmjs.org/` and then `npm ci --prefer-offline` — may work for public deps but not for packages hosted on GHCR.
tony nguyen: for GHCR-hosted private pkgs -> manual workaround: pull node_modules from last successful build artifact and upload to s3, then in workflow download and extract. Steps:
```
# producer
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-ci-cache/node-mods-1.2.3.tgz ./
# consumer in job
aws s3 cp s3://incidents/hotfix/node-mods-1.2.3.tgz ./
tar -xzvf node-mods-1.2.3.tgz -C ./node_modules
```
maria lopez: I can publish a cache tarball from a previous runner (I have a copy). Uploading now to s3://incidents/1930005555/node-mods-hotfix.tgz :arrow_up:
infra-sre-bot: upload complete (size=42MB). object: s3://incidents/1930005555/node-mods-hotfix.tgz
sarah chen: ok let's test the patched workflow on the hotfix branch. I'll push a 1-line PR that adds the s3-download step and sets NODE_ENV=ci to prefer offline installs.
(evans) evan (product): recommend we also prepare a customer note: short, factual, no blame: "We're seeing delays in our build/publish pipelines due to an ongoing GitHub Packages/Actions incident; our engineers have implemented a temporary workaround for impacted customers and are monitoring. We'll update when GH posts status or we have a timeline for full recovery." Would that work?
tony nguyen: yes, that's good. @maria can you draft a CS message and post to #customer-success?
maria lopez: will do after we confirm the hotfix deploy works with the S3 fallback.
(sarah chen edits): PR merged to branch hotfix/s3-fallback (run #57). Starting the rebuilt job.
infra-sre-bot: job logs: runner-1234: fetching s3 artifact... ok
maria lopez: job passed the install step. now running build -> packaging -> docker push is next; docker push goes to GHCR too (ghcr push will fail). we should avoid pushing to GHCR for now; push images to our internal registry at registry.redwood-internal:5000 instead.
tony nguyen: agree — change the push target in the workflow to registry.redwood-internal. I'll open quick patch to replace GHCR_PUSH to INTERNAL_REGISTRY and set `CR_PAT` not required for internal registry.
sarah chen: manual promotion plan if CI still can't push: build image locally and use `rdwctl deploy --image sha` to push via our deployment agent. That bypasses GH Actions pushes entirely. Ops team, are you comfortable with manual deploy? @ops@redwood-support
ops@redwood-support: we can run manual deploys. We'll need the image tarball, SHA, and a brief runbook. Recommend using the `manual-release` channel for coordination.
maria lopez: build + push to internal registry step succeeded on run #57. candidate deployed to canary cluster. smoke tests passing.
evan (product): customer-impact update for execs: 5 customers could have been blocked, we mitigated by using s3 cache + internal registry. No customer-facing rollback required. Severity downgraded to medium. Will prepare executive note.
sarah chen: handing oncall to @tony nguyen — I need to step OOTO for 30m. If GH status updates to resolved, please start reverting temporary patches (remove S3 steps, restore GHCR push) and coordinate a canary rollback of the workflow.
tony nguyen: taking over oncall. I'll watch status and revert when GH confirms recover. Also will run a short post-incident checklist: document changes, PRs to revert, and run an audit to ensure no creds leaked in s3 artifacts. :white_check_mark:
infra-sre-bot: reminder: created incident runbook at https://redwood.internal/incidents/1930005555 - include mitigation steps and artifact links.
maria lopez: posted customer message draft to #customer-success; CS to send after final confirmation.
oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-03-15-01 status changed to monitoring. assigned_to: tony nguyen.
tony nguyen: notes for follow-up:
- add registry fallback/dual-publish support in workflows so we can push to both GHCR and internal registry optionally
- add automated artifact mirroring to S3 after successful builds
- run a dry-run of manual deploy runbook next week
- update runbooks to include GH status link and quick commands to switch registries
sarah chen: thanks all. good catch and fast mitigation. :thumbsup:
maria lopez: closing thread here; will reopen if GH reports recovery and we start revert work.
